description:
We are Stellar Conduct - A team dedicated to making space mission design engaging, accessible, and educational. Our vision is to turn complex ideas into an interactive learning experience. Rather than simply reading about engineering trade-offs, players get to experiment, learn from mistakes, and improve their designs. 

We are computer science students from Malaysia, from Universiti Putra Malaysia Sarawak in Bintulu, we’re here to code solutions that could educate students all around the world.
summary: As humanity prepares for sustained lunar exploration and deep-space missions, NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) serves as the indispensable foundation—mapping safe landing sites, locating vital cryogenic water ice, and characterizing hazardous terrain, illumination limits, and cosmic radiation. However, despite LRO’s critical role in enabling humanity’s return to the Moon, the mission's operational complexities and scientific value remain largely opaque outside aerospace institutions. To bridge this gap, LRO Mission Control—a mobile-ready web simulation—places users directly in command of the orbiter to manage power, fuel, and telemetry while navigating actual lunar hazards. Supported by gamified progression, daily streaks, an in-app Reference Library, a scientific calculator, and the AstroPeers collaborative hub, the platform transforms passive observation into active mission mastery. Simply ensuring the public knows and understands LRO’s vital work sparks genuine curiosity, widens accessible STEM participation, builds informed support for deep-space exploration, and cultivates the systems-thinking skills needed to solve complex resource and climate challenges on Earth.
details:
Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) Mission Control

LRO Mission Control is an interactive, brower-based space mission simulation and gamified educational platform based on NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO). Players step into shoes of a mission controller, experiencing the high-stakes stages of lunar exploration. The game translates complex space science, orbital mechanics, and physics-based problem-solving into a highly engaging, user- friendly dashboard, giving players a hands on understanding of how real lunar exploration missions operate.

KEY TECHNICAL INNOVATIONS

  • Dynamic Mission HUD & Gamified Procedures :
    The dashboard approximates real mission control interfaces, integrating:

    - Interactive Controls: Users manipulate 3x3, 4x4, and 6-switch arrays to execute procedures (e.g. orbital burns or moon captures), constantly managing a real-time fuel gauge.
    - Procedural Tracker : A visual node system provides immediate feedback on current, pending, and completed tasks.
  • Integrated Utility Suite : The platform includes native tools like an engineering calculator for in-game maths challenges and a spatial-audio mission playlist, ensuring users remain immersed in the simulation.
  • AstroPeers Social Simulation : An embedded, simulated social feed mimics real-time coordination with a mission team, promoting collaborative problem-solving concepts.
  • Stellar Economy & Customisation: A points-based virtual economy rewards successful mission execution. Users can utilise points to unlock profile aesthetics, driving user retention and engagement.

MISSION STRUCTURE & GAMEPLAY LOOP

Players command a lunar exploration mission divided into structured, interactive stages that require data interpretation and physics-based problem-solving.

  • Mission 1 : Launch Day: Players configure the launch system, calculate requirements, and manage the launch sequence to achieve escape velocity.
  • Mission 2 : Moon Capture: Users monitor spacecraft telemetry and manage the precise braking manoeuvres (ΔV) required for lunar orbit insertion.

  • Mission 3 : Orbit Shaping: Players adjust orbital parameters, altering altitude and trajectory to establish the optimal mapping orbit.

  • Mission 4 : Mapping Run: Users identify and deploy the correct scientific instruments for specific lunar observation and topographic tasks.

  • Mission 5 : Landing Site: Acting as data analysts, players cross-reference lunar surface slope, boulder hazards, ice availability, and temperature variations to select a viable landing site.

PRESENTING SIMULATION RESULTS & FEEDBACK

  • Adaptive Feedback Systems : As users interact with the controls, varying mission parameters trigger immediate feedback from an animated mascot (the "Hero"), which delivers dynamic, actionable mitigation recommendations via comic-style text bubbles.
  • Result Card Output : Upon mission completion, the platform generates a comprehensive Result Card. Users receive a graded badge, a points payout, and a breakdown of their execution efficiency, providing an audit-ready compliance package of their progress.

EDUCATIONAL IMPACT & GOALS

LRO Mission Control delivers immediate value by reducing the friction in STEM learning and improving cognitive problem-solving skills.

  • Accessible Space Science : By gamifying orbital mechanics and telemetry, the platform flattens the learning curve, making complex data analysis intuitive for students.
  • Interactive Evaluation : The platform bridges the gap between raw NASA lunar exploration data and space science education, providing a fun, interactive, and engaging alternative to static learning.
  • Supporting Educators : The structured, gamified environment provides educators with built-in mechanics to track student comprehension and maintain high engagement levels.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES

By completing the game, players are expected to gain a better understanding of the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter mission and its contribution to lunar exploration. They will also develop basic knowledge of orbital mechanics, scientific instrument, mathematical calculations and lunar landing-site analysis.

Ultimately, LRO Mission Control aims to transforms space science education from a passive lecture into an active, immersive discovery.

STRATEGIC ROADMAP FOR FUTURE EXPANSION

While the current build serves as a robust MVP, the architecture is designed for scalable expansion:

  1. Live NASA API Integration : Transitioning to live data ingestion by connecting to NASA's public LRO telemetry libraries, allowing users to solve challenges based on real-time orbital data.
  2. Multiplayer "Mission Control" Mode : Expanding the AstroPeers feature into a live, co-op multiplayer mode, where students manage different subsystems simultaneously.
  3. Hardware Integration : Exporting web-based logic to interface with IoT hardware, bridging the gap between software simulation and physical engineering.

Use of Nasa Data

The simulation's challenges and parameters are directly informed by authentic NASA resources. We ingested documentation from the Planetary Geodynamics Laboratory (PGDA), LRO Mission Fact Sheets, and Lunar Coordinates Whitepapers to ensure that the instrument loadouts, orbital altitudes, and landing site hazard analyses mirror real-world LRO operations.


TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGIES ARCHITECTURE

Core Logic & Engine :
  • Python: Machine learning (ML) models
  • JavaScript (with Phaser): 2D game development and interactive simulations
  • Vanilla JavaScript: Frontend logic and localStorage (Web Storage API) state management
Frontend & UI :
  • HTML5: Single-page application (SPA) structure
  • CSS3: Flexbox/Grid layouts, custom variables for Light/Dark theming, and keyframe animations
  • Google Fonts: 'Lilita One' and 'Nunito' typefaces
Assets :
  • SVG: Scalable UI components and embedded base64 images
